subject: ComputerScience
sentence: In stored program computers, algorithm and data applications are the same program.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Stored program computers consist of three main parts: the control unit, memory, and the arithmetic logic unit (ALU).

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Stored program computers also have input and output devices, parts we regularly interact with.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Keyboards, mice, and screens are all examples of input and output devices.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: A computer's memory stores all the information it receives.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Computers have one kind of memory, not separate systems.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: The control unit tells the computer what to do.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: The arithmetic logic unit (ALU is a fundamental part of modern computers and acts as the computer's brain.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Modern ALUs have billions of transistors.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Transistors in the ALU can be seen as equivalent to light bulbs.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Computers using the binary system interpret 0 as off and 1 as on.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Modern computers can turn these "lightbulbs" on and off billions of times every second.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Complex operations are possible due to the large number of quick switches transistors can make.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: The binary system allows computers to process large amounts of data and execute algorithms efficiently.
